themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing Across Lower Manhattan
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 300% surge—suggesting a coordinated removal, theft, or maintenance gap affecting wayfinding and pedestrian safety in CD 101.
evidence: 4 street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.0, high severity)
Spike is acute and recent, suggesting either sudden infrastructure failure or coordinated removal rather than long-running degradation
Community Board has repeatedly requested street light repairs, indicating existing infrastructure maintenance gaps in the district
reporting_angles: Are signs being stolen, removed for construction, or neglected by DOT? Check recent DOT work orders.
Interview residents and pedestrians about navigation challenges; photograph affected intersections.

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Complaints Surge in District
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 5 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 1.6 per week—a 208% increase—potentially signaling a contamination event, supplier issue, or inspection gap across multiple food vendors in Lower Manhattan.
evidence: 5 food poisoning complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.04, high severity)
Lower Manhattan has high concentration of food vendors and restaurants serving both residents and tourists—exposure is broad
Community Board has requested public health programs funding, suggesting ongoing health infrastructure concerns
reporting_angles: Request DOH inspection records and violations for restaurants/vendors in affected area over the past 2 weeks.
Interview residents who filed complaints; identify common vendor, supplier, or food type linking incidents.
Check if a specific restaurant chain or supplier has been flagged for violations or recalls.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Cannabis Retailers Operating Unchecked
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints surged 500% LAST WEEK to 3 complaints versus a 0.5 weekly baseline—the highest spike on record—indicating unlicensed or non-compliant cannabis shops proliferating in Lower Manhattan as enforcement lags.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.0, high severity)
Spike emerged suddenly, suggesting either rapid expansion of illegal operations or community awareness of compliance issues
Lower Manhattan's dense retail corridor and high foot traffic make it attractive for unregulated vendors
reporting_angles: Map locations of 311 complaints; are they clustered in specific neighborhoods (e.g., TriBeCa, SoHo, Nolita)?
Interview affected residents about what makes these shops non-compliant—unlicensed, no testing, selling to minors, etc.
Check OCM (Office of Cannabis Management) enforcement records and audit compliance licensing data for the district.

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Complaints Double in One Week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints shot up 154% LAST WEEK to 41 complaints versus a 16.1 weekly baseline—the largest absolute spike among noise types—suggesting a specific event, construction phase, or venue causing sustained disruption.
evidence: 41 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 16.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.53, high severity)
Spike is concentrated and acute rather than creeping, suggesting a temporary but significant source (e.g., major construction, festival, street closure prep)
Noise is the 4th largest complaint category in the district by volume (1,107 total over 90 days), indicating a chronic baseline that was just exceeded
reporting_angles: Identify major construction projects or street work permits filed in the past 1-2 weeks via DOB data or NYC.gov permits.
Check for scheduled events, street fairs, or infrastructure work (e.g., Battery Park City waterfront closure mentioned in Gothamist article).
Interview residents in high-complaint blocks about source and duration of noise; assess enforcement response.

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Crisis in Lower Manhattan
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints exploded 336% TWO WEEKS AGO to 12 complaints versus a 2.8 weekly baseline—the highest z-score (8.49) of all spikes—but the signal has cooled since; investigate what triggered the spike and whether conditions have actually improved or complaints have plateaued.
evidence: 12 air quality complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.49, highest spike in dataset)
Spike is now 2 weeks old and may have resolved, but represents the most severe statistical deviation; unclear if underlying condition improved or residents stopped reporting
Lower Manhattan waterfront redevelopment and Battery Park City flooding prep work (per Gothamist, April 28) may have triggered dust or emissions
reporting_angles: Check EPA AirNow, DEP air quality monitors, and NOAA historical data for the 2-week period; was there an actual air quality event?
Cross-reference with DOB construction permits and DOT work orders to identify dust-generating activity coinciding with the spike.
Interview residents who filed complaints; ask about source, duration, and whether they've noticed improvement—distinguish between real improvement and complaint fatigue.
